Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also raising its prices. The company confirmed to 9to5Mac that Apple TV's monthly fee will increase from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

The Apple One individual plan will also see a price increase.

Apple TV and Apple One both raise prices

Here's the pricing breakdown:

  • Apple TV (monthly): US$14.99 (was US$12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): US$119 (was US$99)
  • Apple One individual plan: US$21.95 (was US$19.95)

Other Apple One plans remain unchanged. When Apple raised Apple Music prices last month, it also raised prices for the Apple One family plan and Apple One Premier plan, but kept the individual plan price unchanged.

New pricing takes effect immediately for new subscribers. Apple said existing subscribers will be notified of the price increase approximately one month before the new pricing takes effect.

The last time Apple raised Apple TV pricing was in August 2025, when the monthly fee went from US$9.99 to US$12.99, while annual plans and Apple One bundle plans were not raised at that time.

Apple has significantly expanded Apple TV's content lineup over the past year. Last October, the company announced it had become the exclusive broadcast partner for F1 (Formula 1) in the United States. The F1 streaming service is included in the standard Apple TV monthly fee at no extra charge.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) streaming to Apple TV at no additional cost. Previously, MLS matches required a separate MLS Season Pass subscription.

Apple has also recently benefited from the successful launch of several shows, such as the fourth season of "Ted Lasso." Season 2 of "Dark Matter" premieres on Apple TV today. Season 6 of "Slow Horses" will premiere on September 16.

What do you think of Apple TV's new pricing? At US$14.99 per month, is Apple TV offering good value for the content provided? Let us know in the comments.
